parsed_artifact.contradiction_resolution: No claim-level contradiction: contradicts_claim_ids is empty, and the statement does not oppose CONJ-0001, THM-0001–THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001. It is compatible with THM-0001 (smooth proper DM stack cohomology is pure of weight equal to degree over Q) and with the campaign’s Q-coefficient exact target W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q). Independent checks. (1) Stack-level torsor: for a smooth curve family C→B, the relative ordered configuration stack of n pairwise-distinct sections is a principal S_n-bundle (finite étale S_n-torsor) over the open of reduced-support degree-n effective divisors in the relative symmetric product/Hilbert scheme; this is the standard configuration geometry used by the packet bottleneck and already recorded as corroborated FND-0064 for n=6 on Conf_6(C/B^{bal}). (2) Coarse failure: a G-torsor is a free G-action with geometric quotient isomorphic to the base; when residual automorphisms of a geometric fibre permute the marked points, the induced S_6-action on ordered configurations is not free relative to the coarse unordered base, so the map of coarse moduli spaces is not a free finite étale S_6-torsor at those points (standard stack-versus-coarse phenomenon for moduli with automorphisms). (3) Rational invariants/coinvariants: for a finite group G and a Q[G]-module V (char 0, |G| invertible), Maschke’s theorem makes Q[G] semisimple, so the averaging projector (1/|G|)∑_{g∈G} g identifies V^G ≅ V_G; thus for Q-cohomology of a finite étale S_6-cover, passage to S_6-invariants equals passage to coinvariants and ordered→unordered descent is harmless. (4) Stack vs coarse rationally: Edidin arXiv:1006.2364v2 (abstract and §4.3) proves that the (functorial/equivariant) cohomology ring of a quotient Deligne–Mumford stack is rationally isomorphic to the cohomology of its coarse moduli space; the same comparison fails integrally, which is why Edidin develops integral stack cohomology separately. Consequently any integral-coefficient or coarse-space C66-TATE-* argument that treats Conf_6→(reduced-support open) as a free S_6-torsor of schemes, or that identifies stack and coarse integral cohomology without further work, is unjustified; rational stack/orbifold cohomology is the correct medium for the campaign’s Q-target. Mild scope note only: the campaign target is already with Q coefficients, so the finding is a method-discipline obstruction (must use stack cohomology and S_6-invariants bookkeeping) rather than a blocker of every rational C66-TATE path that already works on stacks; integral/coarse upgrades remain blocked. Distinct from corroborated FND-0064 (positive stack-torsor existence, not descent discipline), from FND-0051 (Aut(Γ)-invariants/coinvariants for boundary stable-graph strata, different geometric locus), and from FND-0053 (rational irreps of S_6 do not force only Tate local systems on the cover). Do not merge. Promote candidate to corroborated; evidence_class upgraded from adversarial_review to primary_source on independent primary-source verification of the stack torsor, coarse failure at residual automorphisms, Q-invariants≅coinvariants, and Edidin’s rational stack–coarse comparison. Merge target: none.
